title: Pointers & memory
description: Loads, stores, and indirection in 64-bit mode
theory:
## Addresses

Use `lea` for addresses without touching memory; use `mov` with brackets to **dereference**. Keep pointer size at **64 bits** unless you intentionally work in 32-bit domains.

exercises.title: Dereference byte
exercises.description: `.data` defines `x: db 'Q'` and `p: dq x` (pointer to `x`). Load `p` into `rax`, then print the byte at `[rax]` (`Q`, no newline), exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
x: db 'Q'
p: dq x
section .text
_start:
    ; mov rax, [rel p] then write one byte at [rax]
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `mov rax, qword [rel p]` then `mov rsi, rax` for `write`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
x: db 'Q'
p: dq x
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, qword [rel p]
    mov r8, rax
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, r8
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Store through pointer
exercises.description: Reserve one byte in `.bss` at `slot`. Let `ptr` in `.data` be `dq slot`. Store `'Z'` into `slot` **through** `ptr` (two-step: load ptr to reg, `mov byte [reg], 'Z'`). Print `slot` with one-byte `write`, exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .bss
slot: resb 1
section .data
ptr: dq slot
section .text
_start:
    ; mov rax, [rel ptr]; mov byte [rax], 'Z'
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .bss
slot: resb 1
section .data
ptr: dq slot
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, qword [rel ptr]
    mov byte [rax], 'Z'
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel slot]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Pointer arithmetic
exercises.description: Array `db 'M','N','O'`. Let `base` hold its address (`dq arr`). Load pointer, add **2** to point at `'O'`, print that single byte, exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'M','N','O'
base: dq arr
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'M', 'N', 'O'
base: dq arr
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, qword [rel base]
    add rax, 2
    mov r8, rax
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, r8
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Base + index byte
exercises.description: Array `db 'J','K','L'` at `arr`. Put `lea rbx, [rel arr]` in `rbx`, then load the middle byte with `movzx eax, byte [rbx+1]`. Store that ASCII byte into one-byte `.bss` `out`, `write` `out`, exit 0. Expected stdout (trimmed) is `K`.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'J','K','L'
section .bss
out: resb 1
section .text
_start:
    ; lea rbx, [rel arr]; movzx eax, byte [rbx+1]; mov [out], al; write
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `movzx` widens the byte so you can use a 32-bit `add` later if needed — here storing `al` is enough
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'J', 'K', 'L'
section .bss
out: resb 1
section .text
_start:
    lea rbx, [rel arr]
    movzx eax, byte [rbx+1]
    mov [rel out], al
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel out]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
